name: Ashokan Brahmi
diagnosticFeatures: Strictly rectilinear and geometric strokes
Total absence of top headmark (Talakattu)
Basic geometric circle, cross, and vertical bar foundations
Uniform stroke width without calligraphic modulation
significance: First attested written records in Karnataka, marking the foundational root of Indian epigraphy.

sampleGlyphs.label: Foundation Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Rectilinear glyph formed by a vertical spine and two leftward angled arms.

sampleGlyphs.label: Unaspirated Velar Plosive
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Symmetrical orthogonal cross (+) chiseled deeply into coarse granite.

sampleGlyphs.label: Voiced Velar Plosive
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Inverted chevron (^) representing voiced stop without horizontal base closure.

name: Satavahana Brahmi
diagnosticFeatures: Emergence of base curvatures on vertical stems
Incipient triangular thickening or serif at stem tops
Curved horizontal vowel diacritics (Matras)
Modulated chisel pressure visible on limestone
significance: Bridge between North Indian Mauryan Brahmi and regional Deccan epigraphical traditions.

sampleGlyphs.label: Initial Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Beginnings of curvature on lower left hook with upper serif thickening.

sampleGlyphs.label: Velar Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Crossbar exhibits slight curve with terminal chisel indentation.

sampleGlyphs.label: Voiced Velar
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Rounded arch replacing the sharp angle of Mauryan Brahmi.

name: Kadamba (Proto-Kannada)
diagnosticFeatures: Diagnostic box-head (Petika-shirsha / square hollow top mark)
Strong angular geometry with vertical stem terminations
Distinct loop formation in labials (ba, ma, pa)
First appearance of archaic letter Sakata Repha (ಱ)
significance: The cradle of Kannada epigraphy; script of the Halmidi inscription (c. 450 CE).

sampleGlyphs.label: Box-Headed Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Square box-head replaces the simple serif; lower limbs curve decisively.

sampleGlyphs.label: Box-Headed Velar Stop
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Vertical spine crowned by a distinct hollow rectangle chiseled into sandstone.

sampleGlyphs.label: Quadrangular Voiced Stop
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Angular crown with flat shoulders, anticipating curved arch of Chalukya period.

name: Badami Chalukya
diagnosticFeatures: Transition from box-head to horizontal stroke headmark (Proto-Talakattu)
Widely spaced rounded loops in dental and labial glyphs
Serif modulation chiseled deeply into red sandstone
Tripadi poetic metre engraved on cliff faces (Kappe Arabhatta)
significance: Flourishing era of early Kannada metrics and royal prashasti inscriptions.

sampleGlyphs.label: Curvilinear Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Elongated loop with smooth horizontal upper line replacing the square box.

sampleGlyphs.label: Curved Stem Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Left hook displays rounded sweep with modulated chisel depth on red sandstone.

sampleGlyphs.label: Classical Arch
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Broad symmetrical arch with nascent horizontal talakattu serif.

name: Rashtrakuta
diagnosticFeatures: Stable horizontal headmark bar with downward terminal tick
Broad, horizontally expanded glyph proportions
Standardized conjunct consonant ligatures (Ottaksharas)
Classical Old Kannada literary era (Kavirajamarga period)
significance: Peak of pan-Indian Kannada imperial epigraphy across Central and Southern India.

sampleGlyphs.label: Broad Imperial Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Horizontal expansion reflecting calligraphic confidence on imperial copper plates.

sampleGlyphs.label: Proto-Talakattu Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Horizontal top bar shows terminal tick; lower loop fully closed.

sampleGlyphs.label: Symmetrical Velar Arch
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Broad parabolic curve with uniform horizontal headmark stroke.

name: Kalyana Chalukya
diagnosticFeatures: High circularity and fluid curves enabled by soft green soapstone
Clearly delineated V-shaped and hooked talakattu
Complex stacked ligatures (three-consonant conjuncts)
Exquisite calligraphic balance between text and ornamental borders
significance: Introduction of soft chlorite schist soapstone enabling unprecedented calligraphic refinement.

sampleGlyphs.label: Circular Soapstone Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Near-perfect circular arcs carved effortlessly into soft chlorite schist.

sampleGlyphs.label: Florid Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Distinct hooked talakattu with fluidly curving lower terminal loop.

sampleGlyphs.label: Fluid Arch
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Rounded arch with sharply incised upper wedge headmark.

name: Hoysala
diagnosticFeatures: Peak artistic floridity; double loops, recursive curls, decorative flourishes
Sharp V-shaped open Talakattu (✓)
Carved with jewelry-like precision by master sculptors (Ruvari)
Ornate plinth bands on star-shaped temple basements (Belur, Halebidu)
significance: Considered the zenith of Indian epigraphical calligraphy; stone carved like ivory.

sampleGlyphs.label: Ornate Double-Loop Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Double concentric loops terminating in an upward spiral flourish.

sampleGlyphs.label: Master-Sculptor Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Exquisite V-shaped talakattu with delicate recurved decorative tails.

sampleGlyphs.label: Florid Arch
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Broad sweeping arch flanked by ornamental terminal scrollwork.

name: Vijayanagara
diagnosticFeatures: Pragmatic reduction of florid curls for hard granite carving
Stable modern circular loop geometry with clear separation
Consistent open check-mark Talakattu (✓)
Complete divergence of Telugu and Kannada regional orthographic forms
significance: Widespread administrative and religious epigraphy across peninsular India.

sampleGlyphs.label: Granite-Adapted Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Simplified circular contours engineered for durable chisel strokes in granite.

sampleGlyphs.label: Standard Talakattu Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Standard open check-mark talakattu identical to pre-print forms.

sampleGlyphs.label: Circular Arch
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Well-balanced circular arch with crisp top apex mark.

name: Mysuru Wodeyar
diagnosticFeatures: Cursive, continuous loops adapted from iron stylus writing on dried palm leaves
Rounded ligatures avoiding vertical sharp breaks that tear leaf fibres
Direct precursor to 19th-century movable metal type
Bilingual grants in Kannada and Sanskrit with standardized orthography
significance: Direct bridge to modern typographic printing press (Basel Mission, Mangaluru).

sampleGlyphs.label: Manuscript Cursive Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Smooth circular sweep designed not to tear dried palm leaves.

sampleGlyphs.label: Pre-Print Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Direct precursor to 19th-century Basel Mission metal type.

sampleGlyphs.label: Modern-Contour Arch
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Near-identical geometry to contemporary Kannada letter forms.

name: Present Kannada
diagnosticFeatures: Standardized 49-53 character Varnamale
Consistent open check-mark Talakattu (✓)
Standard typographic grid with normalized kerning and baselines
Unicode standard encoding (U+0C80 to U+0CFF)
significance: Standardized modern literary and administrative script of Karnataka.

sampleGlyphs.label: Standardized Unicode Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Normalized baseline, uniform stroke modulation, standard open loop.

sampleGlyphs.label: Standard Typographic Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Standard check-mark talakattu (✓) with calibrated inner kerning.

sampleGlyphs.label: Standard Typographic Arch
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Balanced arch with standard open top talakattu mark.
